title: By the angels standing in perfect rows.
subtitle: Why ranks of angels are sworn by

row.title: a line is just a line
a row is worship
sub: like the angels before their Lord

then: Ibn Masud and many others said these are {idea}the angels{/idea}. Qatadah said they form ranks in the heavens. The Prophet ﷺ told his companions to form rows {idea}as the angels do before their Lord{/idea}: complete the front rows and stand close.
now: You arrive at the mosque and stand at the back with gaps on either side, half thinking about your phone. {idea}The angels are standing in rows too, right now, in the heavens.{/idea} Your row on earth echoes theirs.
old: Where I stand in prayer does not really matter.
new: When I straighten my row, I am standing the way the angels stand.
try: In your next congregational prayer, fill the gap beside you and straighten your line.

title: By the angels who drive the clouds.
subtitle: The unseen workers behind the weather
then: Ibn Masud said these too are {idea}the angels{/idea}. As-Suddi and others said they {idea}drive the clouds.{/idea} For people living in the dry valleys of Makkah, clouds meant rain and life.
now: You check the weather app and grumble at rain on your day off. {idea}Behind every cloud is a command being carried out{/idea}, and the rain is somebody's crop, somebody's drinking water.
old: The weather is just something that happens.
new: Even the clouds are moved by Allah's servants, on His orders.
try: When you see clouds or rain today, say a short thanks for the rain and its blessing.

title: By the angels who bring the reminder.
subtitle: The message came through a chain of trust
then: As-Suddi said {idea}the angels bring the Scriptures and the Quran from Allah to mankind.{/idea} Three oaths by the angels come before the main statement, like a solemn opening before something important is said.
now: The Quran app on your phone sits between a game and a shopping app. It looks like just another app. {idea}The words in it travelled from Allah, through angels, to you.{/idea}
old: The Quran is a book I can open whenever.
new: The Quran is a message brought down by angels, and it reached me.
try: Before you next open the Quran, pause for a second and remember where it came from.

title: Your God is One.
subtitle: What the three oaths were leading to
then: Ibn Kathir says this is the statement the oaths confirm: {idea}there is no god worthy of worship but He.{/idea} The Quraysh worshipped many idols and mocked the Prophet ﷺ for calling to one God.
now: Your boss wants one thing, your parents another, your friends a third, and your feed tells you who to be. {trap}You are pulled in ten directions.{/trap} {idea}One God means one direction.{/idea}
old: I have to keep everyone happy.
new: I only have One to answer to, and that makes life simpler.
try: When you feel torn today, ask: what would please Allah here? Let that decide.

title: Lord of every sunrise.
subtitle: The One God runs the whole sky
then: Ibn Kathir says He is the Sovereign who controls {idea}the stars and planets that rise in the east and set in the west.{/idea} The sun rises from a different point through the year, and He is Lord of each one.
now: Your alarm goes off before dawn. Outside, the sun is coming up from a slightly different spot than last month. {idea}Every single sunrise is under His care{/idea}, including the one that started your day.
old: Sunrise is just the start of another busy day.
new: Each sunrise is placed there by my Lord, and so is my day.
try: Watch the sunrise or the morning light once this week, and say the morning remembrance.

title: The stars are decoration for the nearest sky.
subtitle: Beauty placed for those who look up
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah adorned the lowest heaven {reward}for those on earth who look at it{/reward}, and the stars give them light. He links it to 67:5 and 15:16, where the sky is beautified for the beholders.
now: You have not looked at the night sky properly in months. Streetlights, screens, ceilings. {reward}The decoration is still up there{/reward}, put there for you to see.
old: The sky is just there; I hardly notice it.
new: The stars are a gift of beauty, and I am one of the people they were placed for.
try: Turn off a light tonight and look at the sky for a few minutes.

title: The sky is also guarded against rebel devils.
subtitle: Beauty and protection in the same thing
then: Ibn Kathir says this guards the heaven {idea}as it should be protected{/idea} from every insolent devil. When one tries to eavesdrop on the news in the heavens, {trap}a piercing fire comes and burns him.{/trap}
now: You install security on your phone and lock the front door at night. You protect what matters. {idea}Allah protected His revelation far more carefully{/idea}, so what reached you is clean.
old: Who knows what got mixed into the message over time.
new: Allah guarded His revelation from the start, so I can trust it.
try: Say a'udhu billah before reciting today, asking Allah to guard your heart as He guarded His word.

title: They cannot listen in. They are struck from every side.
subtitle: No way in to the exalted assembly
then: Ibn Kathir says the devils {trap}cannot reach the higher group{/trap}, the angels in the heavens, when they speak of Allah's laws and decrees. They are hit from all directions they try to approach from.
now: A horoscope pops up in your feed. A relative swears by a fortune teller. {idea}The unseen is locked away from them{/idea}, struck from every side. Nobody has a back door into what Allah decrees.
old: Maybe some people really can see what is coming for me.
new: The unseen belongs to Allah, and those who claim it are cut off.
try: Next time a horoscope or prediction shows up, scroll past and say tawakkaltu ala Allah.

title: Driven back, and a lasting punishment ahead.
subtitle: Rebellion gets pushed away
then: Ibn Kathir says the devils are {trap}rejected, repelled and prevented{/trap} from reaching the heaven. In the Hereafter they will have an ongoing punishment, as 67:5 also says.
now: You keep pushing at something you know is wrong: the shortcut at work, the habit you hide. It never quite gets you where you want. {idea}Some doors are shut for a reason.{/idea} Turning back is always open.
old: If I push hard enough, I can get away with it.
new: Going against Allah's order only pushes me further away, so I would rather turn back.
try: Name one thing you keep forcing that you know is not right. Stop pushing at it today.

title: One word snatched, nine lies added.
subtitle: Why stolen whispers are not to be trusted
then: Ibn Abbas said devils once sat listening, then {trap}added nine words of their own{/trap} to every word they heard. When the Prophet ﷺ was sent, {idea}the flaming fire would strike them every time.{/idea}
now: A rumour in the family group has one true detail, so everyone believes the rest. A scam email uses your real name. {trap}One true piece makes the lies feel safe.{/trap}
old: If part of it is true, the rest is probably true too.
new: A little truth is often used to carry a lot of falsehood.
try: Before you forward the next message today, check whether all of it is true.

title: Ask them: are you harder to make, or the heavens?
subtitle: Made of sticky clay, doubting a return

row.title: I am too much to remake

then: Ibn Masud said they {idea}admitted the heavens were harder to create{/idea} than they were. So why deny the resurrection? Mujahid and others said sticky clay is {idea}mud that clings to itself{/idea}, a humble start.
now: Clay stuck to your shoes after a rainy walk, hard to scrape off. That is the material you began from. {idea}The One who built the sky out of nothing is not stretched by you.{/idea}
old: I am too complicated a case for anything to fix.
new: I began as clay, and the One who made the heavens can easily remake me.
try: Touch some soil or clay today and remember where you came from.

title: You were amazed, and they were laughing.
subtitle: Two reactions to the same truth

row.title: they laugh, so it is silly
the laughing is the strange part

then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ was {idea}astounded{/idea} that they denied the resurrection while he was certain of it. Qatadah said he was amazed by {trap}the mockery of the misguided.{/trap}
now: You mention you are fasting or going to pray, and a colleague smirks. You feel small for a moment. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ was laughed at too, over the very same truth.{/idea}
old: If people laugh at my faith, maybe I look foolish.
new: Being mocked for the truth puts me in good company.
try: If someone teases you about your faith today, answer with a calm smile and carry on.

title: Reminded, and still not remembering.
subtitle: When reminders bounce off

row.title: no attention
sub: they do not take it in

then: Ibn Kathir describes them as paying {trap}no attention{/trap} when reminded. They heard the warnings in Makkah again and again. {trap}The words reached their ears and stopped there.{/trap}
now: You have heard the same Friday talk about backbiting many times. You nod, then go back to the group chat. {idea}A reminder only works if you let it in.{/idea}
old: I already know this, so I can tune out.
new: Knowing is not the same as remembering; I need to let it change something.
try: Take one reminder you have heard many times and act on it once today.

title: They see a sign and make it a joke.
subtitle: Mockery as a way to avoid thinking
then: Ibn Kathir says an ayah here means {idea}clear evidence and proof{/idea}. Mujahid and Qatadah said {trap}they make fun of it.{/trap} Laughter was easier than facing what the sign meant.
now: Someone shares a serious point in the chat and you reply with a laughing emoji, because thinking about it is uncomfortable. {trap}A joke can be a door you shut on purpose.{/trap}
old: Laughing it off keeps things light.
new: Sometimes my joke is a way of not facing a sign Allah sent me.
try: The next time you feel like joking away something serious, stop and think about it for one minute first.

title: They called it plain magic.
subtitle: Labelling the truth to avoid it
then: They said, in Ibn Kathir's words, {trap}this you have brought is nothing but plain magic.{/trap} Calling it magic let them ignore what it said without having to answer it.
now: You hear advice you do not like and call it extreme, or old-fashioned, or preachy. {trap}The label saves you from thinking.{/trap} {idea}The question is whether it is true.{/idea}
old: Once I name something as nonsense, I do not have to think about it.
new: A label is not a reply; I owe the truth a real look.
try: Think of one reminder you dismissed with a label. Look at what it actually said.
